battle.name: 克里克戰爭
battle.brief: 一八一三年三月，克里克聯邦的戰士襲擊米姆斯堡，開啟聯邦對南方的第一次大規模遠征。安德魯·傑克遜率民兵與陸軍在阿拉巴馬河流域連戰三場，一八一四年三月攻破馬蹄灣。燧發槍在遠征軍的每一列線上，對弓矛構成了最直接的技術壓制。

kit.name: 燧發槍
kit.history: 擊錘打火比火繩穩。線性列陣的射速和精度都靠它撐著。

countries: 交戰的兩方是美國聯邦與克里克聯邦（Creek Confederacy，即莫斯克格人）。聯邦一方以美國陸軍與州民兵組成遠征軍：田納西州與密西西比領地的民兵由安德魯·傑克遜統率，肯塔基州由艾薩克·謝爾比率領，另有密西西比領地、路易斯安那與弗吉尼亞的分遣隊；聯邦陸軍第五步兵營與砲兵隊是遠征军的骨幹，密西西比領地總督詹姆斯·威爾金森是聯邦在南方的主帥。克里克一方是一個由數十個克里克與考荷克、考維塔等城鎮組成的聯邦，內部存在尖銳分歧：以紅棍派為主的上克里克各鎮主張全面抵抗，下克里克各鎮多數希望談判；上克里克的「克里克先知」威廉·韋瑟福德與軍事首腦彼得·麥昆站在抵抗一線，並得到西北聯盟的特庫姆塞與其兄「先知」的支援，聯軍中還混有切羅基與喬克托的戰士。西班牙在佛羅里達仍保有莫比爾與彭薩科拉，其漁船與走私船隊事實上向內陸的克里克人輸送火藥與槍械；英屬加拿大與西屬佛羅里達之間的邊境貿易網，也讓克里克方能持續取得武器與鉛彈。戰後的克里克人被分為留在原地與遷往密西西比河上游兩部分，聯邦的「克里克之友」切羅基人扮演了居間的角色。
countriesEn: The two sides were the United States on one hand and the Creek Confederacy, that is the Muscogee, on the other. The federal side formed its expeditionary force from the United States Army and the state militias: the Tennessee and Mississippi Territory levies were commanded by Andrew Jackson, Kentucky's by Isaac Shelby, with further detachments from the Mississippi Territory, Louisiana and Virginia. The Fifth Infantry and the artillery of the regular army were the backbone of the expedition, while James Wilkinson, governor of the Mississippi Territory, was the federal commander in the south. The Creek side was a confederation of several dozen Creek towns such as Okfuskee, Coosa and Coweta, and it was divided against itself: the upper towns, where the Red Sticks held sway, wanted all-out resistance, while most of the lower towns preferred negotiation. The Creek Prophet William Weatherford and the military leader Peter McQueen stood at the front of the resistance, supported by Tecumseh and his brother the Prophet of the north-west confederacy, and the war party included Cherokee and Choctaw warriors. Spain still held Mobile and Pensacola in Florida, and its fishing and smuggling fleets in effect carried powder and guns inland to the Creeks; the frontier trade network between British Canada and Spanish Florida let the Creek side keep obtaining weapons and lead. After the war the Creeks were divided between those who stayed and those moved up the Mississippi, and the federal Creeks among the Cherokee acted as intermediaries.
people: 聯邦方面最關鍵的人是安德魯·傑克遜。一八一三年三月之前他是田納西民兵的中校；米姆斯堡之後，他被州長任命為志願兵少將，接掌獨立師，並在十月率軍進入阿拉巴馬。傑克遜的第一批命令包括拆毀未經批准在克里克境內修建的馬路與橋樑，因此觸發了克里克人的報復性襲擊；他隨後以「先發制人」的邏輯組織反擊，事後的軍事檢討則指出他未經授權的越境推進正是衝突升級的關鍵。陸軍與民兵方面，約翰·科克少將統率田納西志願步兵，威廉·科菲中校統率田納西騎兵，費迪南德·克萊伯恩中校統率密西西比騎兵，亞歷山大·卡爾霍恩中校與肯塔基的艾薩克·謝爾比中校分別指揮東肯塔基與賓夕法尼亞、弗吉尼亞分遣隊；約翰·塞維爾與大衛·伯恩中校指揮後方與徵發。密西西比領地總督詹姆斯·威爾金森在1813年2月肖德雷河的一次巡邏中被克里克騎兵擊潰，二十六人陣亡，克里克人隨後包圍美國邊境的三座堡壘，其中兩座在1813年3月被攻下或縱火焚毀，事件成為遠征的導火線之一。克里克方面，威廉·韋瑟福德是「克里克先知」，主張全體克里克人團結抵抗；彼得·麥昆是紅棍派的軍事首腦，在一八一三年秋率領數千戰士北進阿拉巴馬；梅納瓦率領那支著名的數千人戰鬥縱隊，其中包含切羅基與喬克托戰士；黑鷹是上克里克的一個首領，在克里克聯邦內部承擔議價的角色。北克里克的「先知」即特庫姆塞的兄弟，帶著西北聯盟的支援到訪克里克各鎮，鼓動全面抗戰。
peopleEn: The decisive figure on the federal side was Andrew Jackson. Until March 1813 he was a lieutenant-colonel in the Tennessee militia; after Fort Mims he was appointed a brigadier-general of volunteers by the governor, took command of his own brigade, and entered Alabama with his troops in October. Among Jackson's first orders were the demolition of roads and bridges built inside Creek territory without authorisation, which provoked retaliatory raids; he then organised the counter-offensive on the logic of striking first, and the military reviews afterwards identified his unauthorised advance across the border as the key to the escalation. Among the army and militia commanders, Brigadier-General John Cocke led the Tennessee volunteers, Lieutenant-Colonel William Coffee the Tennessee cavalry, Lieutenant-Colonel Ferdinand Claiborne the Mississippi cavalry, and Lieutenants Alexander Carharton and Isaac Shelby the eastern Kentucky and the Pennsylvania-Virginia detachments, while John Sevier and David Burr directed the rear and the foraging parties. James Wilkinson, governor of the Mississippi Territory, lost a patrol to Creek horsemen on the Chaudière in February 1813 with twenty-six men killed; the Creeks then invested three American posts on the frontier, two of which were stormed or burned in March 1813, and that was one of the sparks of the expedition. On the Creek side William Weatherford, the Creek Prophet, pressed the whole people to unite in resistance; Peter McQueen was the military head of the Red Sticks and led several thousand warriors north into Alabama in the autumn of 1813; Menawa led the famous war party that included Cherokee and Choctaw warriors; and Black Hawk was one of the upper Creek chiefs, carrying the weight of negotiation inside the confederacy. The Prophet, brother of Tecumseh, visited the Creek towns with the support of the north-west confederacy and urged them to fight to the end.
kits: 燧發槍在這場戰爭裡同時出現在兩條戰線上，而且兩邊的用法不同。聯邦遠征軍的正裝是一七九五年式斯普林菲爾德 .58 口徑滑膛燧發步槍，這種槍是美國仿照法國的一七七七年型與英國的一七七○年代式所製，配球形鉛彈與紙包定裝藥；一八一二年之後，遠征軍也大量使用各州民兵自備的老式滑膛槍與前裝獵槍，肯塔基與田納西民兵尤其偏愛重至二百磅上下、有效射程二百碼以內的獵槍。遠征軍的騎兵使用卡賓槍與燧發手槍，軍官用一八一一式與一八○九年式燧發手槍，哨兵與警衛用短管滑膛手槍。炮兵是制式的六磅與三磅滑膛野戰炮，能發葡萄彈與霰彈，配山炮與臼炮；一八一四年三月的馬蹄灣之役中，傑克遜把僅有的數門野戰炮拉到高原上，對準用木柵與原木築成的寨牆轟擊，掩護步兵衝鋒。克里克戰士的武器是「貿易槍」：從西班牙與英國商人換來的前裝燧發滑膛槍，也有從美國邊界偷運的滑膛步槍；數量有限而子彈與火藥供應不穩，因此弓、矛與短刀仍然是主力，克里克戰士的慣用武器是長矛、戰斧與獵弓，在近身戰中極為致命。另有數量不多的私有燧發手槍，是克里克人作為榮譽象徵的貴重財物，聯邦軍在戰後的繳獲清單裡也記錄過這些物品。真正左右戰局的是補給：遠征軍的子彈、火藥與口糧靠密西西比河船與陸路車隊運入阿拉巴馬，馬匹在沼澤與長距離行軍中大量倒斃，迫使聯邦軍放棄笨重的六磅炮而更依賴步槍射擊與白刃衝鋒；對克里克人而言，最缺的是持續供應的彈藥，一旦商船被封鎖，幾百支貿易槍就會在幾個月內變成無用的木棍。
kitsEn: The flintlock musket appeared on both fronts in this war, and each side used it differently. The regulation arm of the federal expedition was the 1795-pattern Springfield .58-calibre smoothbore flintlock musket, copied in the United States from the French 1777 pattern and the British pattern of the 1770s, firing round lead ball and paper cartridges; after 1812 the expedition also made heavy use of old smoothbores and fore-end-loading rifles supplied by the state militias, the Kentucky and Tennessee men in particular favouring heavy rifles of some two hundred pounds weight with an effective range inside two hundred yards. The cavalry carried carbines and flintlock pistols, officers the 1811 and 1809 patterns of flintlock pistol, and sentries short-barrelled smoothbore pistols. The artillery was the regulation six- and three-pounder smoothbore field gun firing canister and grape, with mountain howitzers and bombs; in the battle of Horseshoe Bend in March 1814 Jackson hauled the few field guns he had up onto the heights and fired them at the breastworks of logs and timber to cover the infantry assault. The Creek warriors carried trade guns, fore-end-loading flintlock smoothbores obtained from Spanish and British traders, as well as smoothbore muskets run across the American border; numbers were limited and the supply of ammunition and powder was uncertain, so the bow, the lance and the short knife remained their main weapons, the lance, the tomahawk and the hunting bow being what a Creek warrior used in close fighting, and deadly. A small number of private flintlock pistols were held as marks of honour and of wealth, and they appear in the federal lists of captured property. What really decided the campaign was supply. The expedition drew its ammunition, powder and rations up the Mississippi River and in by wagon, horses died by the hundred in the swamps and on the long marches, and the federal army was obliged to leave its heavy six-pounders behind and rely more and more on musket fire and on the bayonet; on the Creek side the binding constraint was a continuous supply of ammunition, for once the coastal traders were cut off a few hundred trade guns became sticks within a few months.
tactics: 聯邦軍的戰術可以拆成三段。搜索與追擊：傑克遜堅持情報先行，審訊俘虜、偵察火堆與足跡；他的部隊多在夜間行軍、沿溪流與沼澤邊緣推進，以避開克里克戰士的伏擊，主要道路上的正面推進被壓縮到最小。包圍與固定：到一八一三年十一月的塔盧沙奇之戰，傑克遜命令部隊以步兵方陣圍住村落，隊形層層相疊，從四面同時進逼，迫使聚落中的戰士只能近身；繳獲的战利品被集中在樹下，士兵被要求不得離開戰利品太遠，這條紀律要求同時是防止克里克人奪回裝備的手段。強攻與火力準備：在塔拉迪加，傑克遜利用地形把部隊排成縱隊，命令騎兵在敵陣前製造聲勢與塵土，白人軍官在陣前吹笛鼓噪以渲染聲勢，卻不立即進攻；待克里克戰陣出現鬆動，傑克遜才下令全軍衝鋒。克里克人則偏好游擊與伏擊：在沼澤、密林與溪流之間反覆襲擾聯軍的行軍縱隊與輜重，切斷糧道；在村落中依托木柵、屋牆與樹叢防守，消耗進攻方的銳氣。一八一四年三月二十七日的馬蹄灣之役是最典型的攻堅：傑伊·詹姆斯率領的精銳利用河水暴漲，繞過正面，從後方登上高原，發現對手背水扎營、營寨背後即是陡峭岩壁之後隨即發動攻擊，克里克人被逼入河中或被合圍，指挥官梅納瓦負傷被俘。戰後傑克遜在此地設立了紀念碑。戰爭的後期是圍困與強制遷徙：隨著一個個城鎮被攻下，克里克人陸續向南與西南方向逃亡，最終在1836年依《印第安人遷移法》被強制遷往俄克拉何馬。
tacticsEn: The federal method can be broken into three stages. First, search and pursuit: Jackson insisted on intelligence first, interrogating prisoners and reading the smoke of campfires and the trails; his troops marched mostly at night and along the edges of creeks and swamps to avoid ambush, and frontal movement on the main roads was kept to a minimum. Second, encirclement and fixing: by the battle of Tallushatchee in November 1813 he ordered his infantry to surround the villages in a square formation, layer upon layer, pressing in from all four sides so that the warriors in the settlement were forced into hand-to-hand fighting; the captured booty was piled under the trees and the men were forbidden to stray far from it, a discipline that was also the means of preventing the Creeks from taking their own property back. Third, assault preparation and fire: at Talladega Jackson drew the troops up in column, ordered the cavalry to make noise and dust in front of the enemy position and had the white officers blow pipes and beat drums in front of the line to raise the impression of an approaching host, without attacking; only when the Creek formation showed signs of loosening did he order the general advance. The Creeks in turn preferred skirmish and ambush, harassing the marching columns and the baggage train again and again among the swamps, woods and creeks and cutting the food route, and defending in villages behind palisades, house walls and thickets so as to wear down the attacker. The assault at Horseshoe Bend on 27 March 1814 is the clearest case. A picked force under General John Coffee took advantage of the risen river to get round the position, climbed the bluff and found the camp set with its back to the rock, then attacked at once; the Creeks were driven into the river or surrounded, and their commander Menawa was wounded and taken prisoner. Jackson set up a monument on the field afterwards. The closing phase of the war was the siege and the forced removal: as one town after another fell, the Creeks fled south and south-west, and in 1836 they were forcibly moved to Indian Territory under the Indian Removal Act.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。克里克聯邦的人口約兩萬至三萬人，能徵集的戰士通常被估為八千至一萬五千人；一八一三年秋北上的紅棍派軍隊，學界一般給出六千至八千人。聯邦方面，一八一三年十月傑克遜接任時的遠征軍約九千人，到一八一四年三月馬蹄灣之役時，作戰兵力約三千四百至三千六百人，連同後勤與支援船隻的總數遠高於此。傷亡數字方面，一八一三年三月三十日的米姆斯堡之戰，克里克攻擊方投入約一千五百至一千八百名戰士，堡內守軍約五百人，其中約三百人戰死、二百五十至三百人被俘，守軍的家屬亦在堡內；此役是克里克戰爭中最慘烈的損失。十月三日同一天發生的兩場戰鬥中，塔盧沙奇之役聯邦軍一千二百至一千三百人對克里克戰士約六百至八百人，克里克方面約三百人戰死、二百多人被俘，聯邦軍傷亡數十人；塔拉迪加之役聯邦軍約一千八百人對克里克軍約一千人，克里克方面約三百人戰死，聯邦軍傷亡不到二百人。一八一四年三月二十七日馬蹄灣之役，聯邦軍約三千四百至三千六百人對克里克軍約一千人，克里克方面戰死約三百人、被俘約八百人，另有約二百五十人溺斃，聯邦軍傷亡約一百至二百人，俘獲馬匹數百匹。土地條款是最硬的數字：一八一四年八月二十四日《福特傑克森條約》割讓約二千三百萬英畝土地，約合今日阿拉巴馬州大部與喬治亞州西北部。時間跨度：自一八一三年三月三十日米姆斯堡起至一八一四年八月二十四日條約，約十七個月。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The Creek Confederacy had a population of some twenty to thirty thousand, and the warriors it could raise are usually put at eight to fifteen thousand; the Red Stick force that moved north in the autumn of 1813 is generally given by scholars as six to eight thousand men. On the federal side the expedition numbered about nine thousand men when Jackson took command in October 1813, and the field force at Horseshoe Bend in March 1814 was some three thousand four hundred to three thousand six hundred, with the total including rear-echelon men and support boats far higher. On casualties, in the battle of Fort Mims on 30 March 1813 the Creek attack is put at some fifteen hundred to eighteen hundred warriors against a garrison of some five hundred, of whom about three hundred were killed and two hundred and fifty to three hundred taken prisoner, the families of the garrison being inside the fort as well; that action cost the Creeks more than any other in the war. In the two actions fought on the same day in October, at Tallushatchee twelve hundred to thirteen hundred federal troops met six to eight hundred Creek warriors, of whom about three hundred were killed and more than two hundred taken prisoner, with federal losses of only several dozen; at Talladega some eighteen hundred federal troops engaged about a thousand Creek warriors, about three hundred of whom were killed, while federal casualties numbered fewer than two hundred. At Horseshoe Bend on 27 March 1814 three thousand four hundred to three thousand six hundred federal troops faced about a thousand Creeks, who lost some three hundred killed and about eight hundred captured, with a further two hundred and fifty drowned; federal losses were a hundred to two hundred, and several hundred horses were taken. The hardest number of all is the land: the Treaty of Fort Jackson of 24 August 1814 ceded about twenty-three million acres, the bulk of present-day Alabama together with north-western Georgia. In time, the war ran from Fort Mims on 30 March 1813 to the treaty of 24 August 1814, some seventeen months.
cause: 起因有遠因也有近因。遠因是美國西進拓殖對克里克人土地與貿易的持續擠壓：一七八三年《西北土地法令》之後，喬治亞與田納西的定居者不斷沿克里克河與阿拉巴馬河向上游移動，克里克聯邦被迫在十九世紀初一次又一次割讓土地；一八一一年田納西州議會取得聯邦許可「獲得切羅基與克里克人的土地」的權利，同年十月田納西民兵首領在聯邦默許下進入克里克境內，收繳克里克人的玉米地與牛群，第一批武裝衝突就此爆發。克里克聯邦內部也在一八一二年前後爆發內戰：克里克先知威廉·韋瑟福德與彼得·麥昆在上克里克各鎮推動一場「土地回購」的改革，要用克里克聯邦的公共資金回購並分配被轉讓給美國的土地，這在下克里克各鎮眼中等於是向美國投降；紅棍派武裝起來對抗，得到西北聯盟的特庫姆塞支持，後者在一八一三年初造訪克里克各鎮，鼓動全面抗戰。近因是一八一三年二月的肖德雷河事件：密西西比領地總督威爾金森的巡邏隊在河道被克里克騎兵擊潰，二十六人陣亡，克里克人隨後包圍美國邊境的三座堡壘，其中兩座在三月被攻下或縱火焚毀，三月三十日米姆斯堡之戰隨即爆發，成為聯邦遠征的導火線。必須說明的是，這場戰爭在美國的歷史書寫中長期被歸入「安德魯·傑克遜的戰爭」與「西部拓殖的史觀」，而近年的國家公園與紀念地則更傾向以克里克人的抵抗與自治權的觀點重述這段歷史，這也是同一場戰爭在兩種官方敘事裡得到完全相反評價的原因。
causeEn: There were remote and immediate causes. The remote cause was the steady pressure of American westward settlement on Creek land and trade: after the Northwest Ordinance of 1783 settlers in Georgia and Tennessee moved steadily up the Creek and Alabama rivers, and the Creek Confederacy was forced to cede land again and again in the early nineteenth century; in 1811 the Tennessee legislature obtained federal leave to acquire the lands of the Cherokee and the Creeks, and in October of that year Tennessee militia leaders entered Creek territory with the connivance of the federal authorities, confiscating cornfields and cattle, and the first armed clashes followed. The Creek Confederacy itself was torn by civil war in the years around 1812: the Creek Prophet William Weatherford and Peter McQueen pressed forward in the upper towns a movement to buy back the lands already ceded to the United States with the public funds of the confederacy, which the lower towns read as surrender to the Americans; the Red Sticks armed themselves against them, with the support of Tecumseh, who visited the Creek towns in the early months of 1813 and urged them to fight to the end. The immediate cause was the action on the Chaudière in February 1813: a patrol of Governor Wilkinson's was cut up by Creek horsemen in the creek with twenty-six men killed, after which the Creeks invested three American posts on the frontier, two of which fell or were burned in March; the battle of Fort Mims followed on 30 March 1813 and became the spark of the federal expedition. It should be said that in American historical writing this war has long been filed under the history of Andrew Jackson and of western expansion, while in recent decades the national parks and memorials have tended to retell it from the standpoint of Creek resistance and Creek sovereignty, and that the same war receives opposite verdicts in the two official narratives for exactly that reason.
impact: 影響是克里克民族自治的崩解與南部土地結構的重塑。《福特傑克森條約》之後，克里克聯邦喪失阿拉巴馬河谷的兩千三百萬英畝土地，成為美國建國史上最大規模的單一割讓；克里克人被分為保留地居民與西遷者，西部壓力沿著一八三〇年《印第安人遷移法》的軌道在1836年被推至俄克拉何馬，其後在阿拉巴馬與喬治亞境內的克里克族裔仍作為公民存在，但土地與自治早已不復存在。密西西比領地的棉花種植在一八一〇年代之後沿黑土帶快速擴張，而黑奴的進口正是聯邦遠征軍得以在南方迅速補充兵力的原因，這條「棉花—奴隸—西部」的鏈條在克里克戰爭之後加速成形。軍事的影響同樣具體：這是美國陸軍第一次以志願民兵為主體的大規模遠征，暴露了民兵裝備落後、指揮統一困難、補給線脆弱等問題，直接推動了一八一六年陸軍的擴編與西點軍校的設立；而傑克遜在戰後因戰果與戰術激進受到華盛頓的批評，一八一四年辭去師長職務。文化上，這段歷史在二十世紀後期經歷了一輪重估：聯邦政府把馬蹄灣立為國家公園（一九六四年），克里克人的口述傳統被學者整理出版；與此同時，遠征軍使用的武器——一七九五年式滑膛燧發步槍——也成為大量民用前裝獵槍的原型，其在美國民間延續使用至今仍可在黑火藥射擊運動中見到。長期看，克里克戰爭是「美國西進」敘事中最暴力的一段，之後南方各州的地方法律與聯邦的《印第安人遷移法》把這種壓力制度化，直到二十世紀才被逐步推翻。
impactEn: The effect was the destruction of Creek autonomy and a reshaping of the land structure of the south. After the Treaty of Fort Jackson the Creek Confederacy lost twenty-three million acres of the Alabama valley, the largest single cession in the history of the United States; the Creeks were divided into those who stayed on the reservation and those who moved west, and the pressure of the west carried along the track of the Indian Removal Act of 1830 reached Indian Territory in 1836, though Creek communities in Alabama and Georgia survived afterwards as citizens, having long lost both land and self-government. Cotton planting in the Mississippi Territory expanded quickly along the black belt after the 1810s, and the importation of enslaved people was precisely what allowed the federal expedition to replenish its troops in the south quickly, so that the chain of cotton, slavery and the west hardened after the Creek War. The military consequences were equally concrete: this was the first large federal expedition in which volunteer militia formed the bulk of the army, and it exposed the poor equipment of the militia, the difficulty of unified command and the fragility of the supply line, directly prompting the expansion of the regular army in 1816 and the founding of the West Point Academy. Jackson's aggressive conduct drew criticism in Washington, and he resigned his command in 1814. Culturally, the story was rewritten in the later twentieth century: the federal government made Horseshoe Bend a national park in 1964, and Creek oral traditions were collected and published by scholars. At the same time the weapon the expedition carried, the 1795-pattern smoothbore flintlock musket, became the prototype of a great many civilian fore-end-loading rifles, and the civilian use of such arms continues in the black-powder shooting sports to this day. In the long run the Creek War is the most violent passage in the narrative of American westward expansion, after which the statutes of the southern states and the federal Removal Act institutionalised that pressure, and it was not until the twentieth century that the process was gradually undone.
result: 結果是克里克聯邦的軍事失敗與主權的喪失。一八一四年三月二十七日馬蹄灣之役之後，紅棍派的戰鬥中樞被摧毀，梅納瓦被俘，韋瑟福德率殘部退往紅雲堡，最終於一八一四年向傑克遜投降；一八一四年五月紅雲之役，密西西比騎兵與田納西步兵在紅雲堡對面擊潰克里克與切羅基聯軍；一八一四年八月，在傑克遜回到密西西比領地之後，以紅棍派為首的克里克各派代表在福特傑克森與聯邦簽訂和約，克里克方面承認割讓約二千三百萬英畝土地，承諾分批遷往密西西比河上游的新居地，並接受聯邦的「克里克之友」切羅基人作為居間。克里克人此後又花了二十多年遷徙，1836年最後一批被強制遷往俄克拉何馬。戰爭的技術結果則是：在火器已經全面換裝燧發槍的年代，克里克戰士仍以弓矛為主要手段，因而在面對線性列陣的滑膛槍兵時付出極大代價；反過來說，燧發槍的耐雨性與快速點火，使聯邦遠征軍得以在春秋季的濕冷天候中保持可用的射擊節奏，這是克里克方最難以抵禦的技術差距。最終，聯邦遠征軍並沒有靠一次戰役徹底消滅克里克民族，其「完成」是靠條約、分割與強迫遷徙完成的——這正是這場戰爭在今天仍具爭議的原因。
resultEn: The result was the military defeat of the Creek Confederacy and the loss of its sovereignty. After Horseshoe Bend on 27 March 1814 the fighting heart of the Red Sticks was broken, Menawa was taken prisoner, and Weatherford withdrew with the remnants to Red Cloud, where he eventually surrendered to Jackson in 1814. In the action at Red Cloud in May 1814 the Mississippi cavalry and Tennessee infantry broke the Creek and Cherokee confederate force opposite the redoubt. In August 1814, after Jackson had returned to the Mississippi Territory, representatives of the several Creek parties, the Red Sticks among them, concluded a treaty of peace with the United States at Fort Jackson: the Creeks acknowledged the cession of about twenty-three million acres, undertook to remove by stages to new lands up the Mississippi, and accepted the federal Creeks among the Cherokee as intermediaries. The removal took the Creeks more than twenty years to complete, the last being forced to Indian Territory in 1836. The technical outcome of the war was this: at a time when firearms had moved over entirely to flintlock, Creek warriors still fought mainly with bow and lance, and they paid dearly for it when they met linear formations of smoothbored muskets; conversely, the flintlock's resistance to wet weather and its quick ignition allowed the federal expedition to keep a usable rate of fire through the wet and cold of the spring and autumn campaigns, and that was the technical gap the Creeks could least bridge. In the end the federal expedition did not destroy the Creek nation by any single battle: what finished the war was treaty, division and forced removal, and that is why the Creek War remains a contested chapter to this day.
